# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

## 1. Purpose and Scope

This narrative defines the control, alarm, and safety-shutdown functionality for ammonia screw compressor C-101 and its interface to the machine room ammonia detection and emergency ventilation systems. It is intended as the basis for PLC/HMI programming and for Factory Acceptance Test (FAT) procedures. Each numbered requirement is written to be individually testable.

**Equipment covered:** C-101 (400 hp screw compressor, across-the-line soft starter, slide valve capacity control 10-100%, no VFD), EF-201 (emergency exhaust fan), XV-120 (machine room main liquid solenoid), AE-110A/B (ammonia detectors), and the break-glass emergency stop station.

**Platform:** Allen-Bradley CompactLogix PLC; operator interface on the HMI in the engine room office.

## 2. Instrument and I/O Summary

| Tag | Description | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-101 | Suction pressure | AI, psig | Capacity control variable; low suction trip |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure | AI, psid | Low alarm / low trip |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature | AI, °F | High alarm / high trip |
| II-104 | Motor current (CT) | AI, % FLA | Load limiting |
| AE-110A/B | Ammonia detectors | AI, ppm | Two-stage alarm |
| XV-120 | Machine room main liquid solenoid | DO | Energized = open (fail-closed) |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan | DO, high speed | Started on detector alarm |
| C-101 start/run | Soft starter command / run feedback | DO / DI | |
| SV load / SV unload | Slide valve pulse outputs | DO | |
| Break-glass ESD | Hardwired emergency stop | DI (hardwired) | Also in the motor/xv-120 safety circuit |

## 3. Definitions

- **Trip:** Immediate compressor stop requiring operator reset after the condition clears. Trips latch.
- **Alarm:** Annunciation only, with no equipment action unless stated. Alarms are acknowledged by the operator and clear automatically when the condition returns to normal (past deadband).
- **Emergency shutdown (ESD):** Stop of all compressors plus de-energizing of XV-120.

## 4. Operating Modes

C-101 has HAND/OFF/AUTO selection at the HMI.

- **OFF:** Compressor will not run. Slide valve is unloaded if the unit is stopped.
- **HAND:** Operator starts/stops from the HMI and manually loads/unloads the slide valve. All trips, interlocks, the 95% FLA limit, and the start limiter remain active. Manual loading is inhibited above the current limit.
- **AUTO:** Start/stop and capacity are controlled by the PLC from suction pressure (Section 7).

## 5. Start Permissives

C-101 may start only when all of the following are true. The HMI shall display the first-out/unsatisfied permissive.

1. No active latched trip, and all trips reset.
2. No active ESD (break-glass healthy, no 150 ppm detector condition latched).
3. Slide valve confirmed at minimum position (unloaded).
4. Suction pressure PT-101 above the low-suction trip setpoint plus deadband (above 2 psig + 1 psi = 3 psig, to prevent immediately re-tripping).
5. Start-limiter satisfied (Section 6).
6. Soft starter reports ready/no fault.
7. Instruments healthy (no analog signal fault on PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104).
8. Oil pump or lubrication system ready, if applicable to the packaged unit (confirm against vendor package drawings).

## 6. Start Sequence and Start Limiter

6.1 On a valid start command (AUTO demand or HAND start), the PLC verifies the permissives, then issues the soft starter run command.

6.2 The slide valve shall remain at minimum during start and shall not be allowed to load until the compressor run feedback has been true for an adjustable delay (default 10 s, to be confirmed with the package vendor).

6.3 **Low oil trip bypass:** The low oil differential trip (25 psid) is bypassed for 30 s after the start command (timer starts at the start command). The low oil alarm is also suppressed during this period (assumption; confirm with owner). After 30 s the trip is enabled; if PDT-102 is below 25 psid at that moment, the unit trips immediately. All other trips are active during the bypass window.

6.4 **Start limiter (max 4 starts per hour):** The PLC maintains a rolling 60-minute record of start commands. A start is blocked if four starts have already occurred in the preceding 60 minutes. The HMI shall display "Start inhibited, starts/hour limit" and the time remaining until the next permitted start. A start is counted when the start command is issued, regardless of whether the unit reaches run. The limiter applies in HAND and AUTO. It shall not be resettable by operators at any login level lower than supervisor; any override must be logged. The rolling count shall survive a PLC power cycle (use retentive memory or a timestamp record), since the soft starter's thermal limit is unaffected by PLC restarts. Confirm with the soft starter manufacturer whether the limit counts starts or is thermally modelled.

6.5 If run feedback is not received within an adjustable time (default 5 s) of the start command, the PLC drops the command, annunciates "Failed to start", and the attempt counts toward the start limit.

## 7. Capacity Control (AUTO)

7.1 **Control variable:** Suction pressure PT-101.

7.2 **Setpoint:** 15 psig default, adjustable 5-30 psig. Changes require supervisor login; the HMI rejects entries outside the range and logs each change with user and time.

7.3 **Control action:** The slide valve is moved by pulse outputs. The PLC compares PT-101 to setpoint:
- PT-101 above setpoint plus deadband: pulse the load output.
- PT-101 below setpoint minus deadband: pulse the unload output.
- Within the deadband: no pulse.

Pulse width, interval between pulses, and deadband shall be adjustable (engineering access). Suggested starting values: deadband ±1.0 psi, pulse 0.5-1 s, interval 5-10 s, to be tuned at commissioning. Pulse rate may be scaled in proportion to the error (longer or more frequent pulses further from setpoint), at the integrator's discretion, but must be documented. Whether the integrator uses a PID with pulse conversion or a banded step approach shall be stated in the submittal.

7.4 **Slide valve limits:** The slide valve command range is 10-100%. Loading pulses are not issued at 100%; unloading pulses are not issued at 10%. If slide valve position feedback is not provided, position shall be estimated from accumulated pulse time with a periodic full-unload re-synchronization at each stop. (Confirm whether the package provides a position transmitter.)

7.5 **Motor current limit:** Loading is not permitted when II-104 is at or above 95% FLA.
- At or above 95% FLA: load pulses are inhibited ("Load inhibited, current limit").
- Above a higher threshold, adjustable (suggested 100% FLA), the PLC shall pulse unload until the current falls below 95% FLA. The owner should confirm this threshold.
- The motor current limit holds unless it conflicts with low suction pressure considerations: it takes precedence over the suction pressure demand to load. A sustained high suction pressure under current limit shall raise an alarm after an adjustable delay.
- During the start period, current is ignored for limit and unload action for an adjustable time (default 10 s) to avoid responding to inrush. Overcurrent protection is separate and is provided by the soft starter/motor protection relay, not by this logic.

7.6 **Unload on alarm (recommended):** On TT-103 high alarm or PDT-102 low alarm, the PLC shall inhibit loading. Owner to confirm whether active unloading is also required.

7.7 **Auto start/stop:** Where AUTO start/stop is used, the PLC starts C-101 when PT-101 exceeds setpoint plus an adjustable start differential for an adjustable time, and stops C-101 after the slide valve has been at minimum with PT-101 below setpoint minus a stop differential for an adjustable time. Differentials shall be set so the start limiter is not routinely reached. Default values to be agreed with the owner.

7.8 **Normal stop:** The slide valve is driven to minimum (unload) before the compressor stop command is issued (timeout default 60 s, after which the compressor stops anyway and the alarm "Unload timeout" is raised). In a trip, the unit stops immediately and the slide valve is unloaded after stopping.

## 8. Protective Trips (C-101 only)

| ID | Condition | Alarm | Trip | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Oil differential pressure PDT-102 low | 35 psid | 25 psid | Trip bypassed 30 s after start; trip delay (default 3 s) to filter transients |
| T2 | Discharge temperature TT-103 high | 190 °F | 210 °F | |
| T3 | Suction pressure PT-101 low | (alarm optional, suggested 4 psig) | 2 psig | Trip delay (default 5 s); active after the start period only if the unit cannot otherwise start at low pressure (confirm) |
| T4 | Instrument failure (out-of-range signal, 4-20 mA below 3.6 mA or above 21 mA) on PDT-102, TT-103, PT-101 | Alarm | Trip | Treated as a trip, since the protective function is lost |
| T5 | Soft starter fault / run feedback lost | Alarm | Trip | |
| T6 | Break-glass ESD | | ESD | Hardwired |

8.1 Trips are latched and require the cause to clear, then an operator reset at the HMI. Resetting does not restart the compressor. The HMI shall record first-out cause with a time stamp.

8.2 Alarms have an adjustable deadband (default 2% of span) and delay (default 5 s) to avoid chatter.

8.3 Trip setpoints are configured by engineering/supervisor login only. Trip setpoints shall be fixed to the values above on delivery.

8.4 Setpoints for trips shall not be adjustable by operators. Alarm setpoints shall be within the limits of the corresponding trip.

## 9. Ammonia Detection and Emergency Response

9.1 **Detectors:** AE-110A and AE-110B monitor the machine room. The higher of the two readings is used for each stage (any-one-of-two voting), unless the owner requires 2oo2 voting, which should be confirmed. A detector fault (signal out of range) raises an alarm. A fault on one detector does not disable the other; a fault on both detectors raises a high-priority alarm. The owner shall decide whether both detectors failed should be treated as a shutdown.

9.2 **Stage 1: 25 ppm alarm:**
- Annunciate on the HMI with audible/visual alarm in the engine room office and at the machine room entrance (if beacon provided).
- Start EF-201 in high speed.
- No compressor action.
- The fan stays running until the reading falls below 20 ppm (adjustable) and the operator resets/acknowledges, or per owner preference for a minimum run time. The fan run is latched until operator reset to avoid cycling.

9.3 **Stage 2: 150 ppm shutdown:**
- Stop all compressors (C-101 and any other compressors on the PLC, or via the hardwired ESD circuit).
- De-energize XV-120 (closes the machine room main liquid solenoid).
- EF-201 runs at high speed (it should already be running from Stage 1; the PLC shall command it on directly if the 150 ppm condition is reached without the alarm having started it).
- The ESD condition is latched; the reset requires the ammonia concentration to fall below the alarm level (25 ppm) and a manual reset at the HMI (and at the break-glass station, which must be physically reset).
- Annunciate as a critical alarm.

9.4 **Break-glass ESD station (outside the machine room):** Hardwired, normally closed contact, so that a wire break also initiates ESD. It de-energizes the XV-120 circuit and removes the run permissive or stop signal to compressors independent of the PLC (hardwired to the soft starter control circuit and XV-120 supply). It is also read by the PLC as a status input for annunciation and for starting EF-201 at high speed (confirm the owner's expectation for the fan; this narrative assumes the fan starts on break-glass). The ESD function must work with the PLC powered off or faulted. The integrator shall provide a schematic showing this.

9.5 After an ESD, restarting the compressors is manual only. No automatic restart. XV-120 re-energizes only after the ESD is reset and an operator command (or a delayed re-open if the owner prefers; default is manual).

## 10. Power Loss and Restart

10.1 Upon a loss of power, C-101 stops, and XV-120 closes (fail-closed).
10.2 After power is restored, no automatic restart. The unit remains stopped until the operator or AUTO demand is received, respecting the start limiter and permissives. The owner can opt for an automatic restart with a delay (default: none).
10.3 Alarms and trip states, as well as the start timestamps, shall be retained over a PLC power cycle.

## 11. HMI Requirements

- Overview screen: C-101 status (stopped/starting/running/tripped), mode, PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104, slide valve position/state, setpoint, EF-201 status, XV-120 status, detector readings.
- Alarm banner with time stamp, acknowledge, and an alarm history. First-out trip indication.
- Access levels: Operator (start/stop, acknowledge, reset trips); Supervisor (suction setpoint, alarm setpoints); Engineering (trip setpoints, timers, pulse tuning, calibration).
- Trending of PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104, slide valve, and detector ppm, with retention for at least 30 days.
- Logging of setpoint changes, resets, and bypasses.

## 12. Alarm and Trip Summary

| Condition | Priority | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Ammonia ≥ 25 ppm | High | Alarm; EF-201 high speed |
| Ammonia ≥ 150 ppm | Critical | ESD; all compressors stopped; XV-120 closed; EF-201 on |
| Break-glass activated | Critical | ESD as above |
| PDT-102 < 35 psid | High | Alarm; inhibit loading |
| PDT-102 < 25 psid (after 30 s) | Critical | C-101 trip |
| TT-103 > 190 °F | High | Alarm; inhibit loading |
| TT-103 > 210 °F | Critical | C-101 trip |
| PT-101 < 2 psig | Critical | C-101 trip |
| II-104 ≥ 95% FLA | Medium | Load inhibited |
| Start limit reached | Medium | Start blocked |
| Failed to start / run feedback lost | High | Trip / alarm |
| Instrument fault | High | Trip (protective inputs) / alarm |

## 13. FAT Test Checklist

Test by simulation of inputs (force or signal injection). Record the result and witness initials for each.

| # | Test | Expected result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Start with a trip active | Start blocked; permissive shown |
| 2 | Start with the slide valve not at minimum | Start blocked |
| 3 | Valid start | Soft starter command issued; run feedback; slide valve loading delay observed |
| 4 | Start four times in 60 min, attempt a fifth | Fifth blocked; time remaining displayed; restored after the oldest start ages out |
| 5 | Cycle PLC power after four starts | Start limit still enforced |
| 6 | Hold PDT-102 at 30 psid within 30 s of start | No trip |
| 7 | Hold PDT-102 at 30 psid after 30 s | Alarm at 35 psid; trip at 25 psid (after delay), latched |
| 8 | Hold PDT-102 at 20 psid at the start; keep until 30 s | Trip at 30 s |
| 9 | Ramp TT-103 to 190 °F, then 210 °F | Alarm, then trip; loading inhibited at alarm |
| 10 | Ramp PT-101 down to 2 psig | Trip, latched |
| 11 | Vary PT-101 above and below the 15 psig setpoint | Load pulses above, unload pulses below, none in the deadband |
| 12 | Change setpoint as operator, then as supervisor; enter 4 and 31 psig | Operator denied; supervisor accepted in range, out-of-range rejected; changes logged |
| 13 | Raise II-104 to 95% FLA while PT-101 demands loading | Load pulses inhibited; message shown |
| 14 | Raise II-104 above the unload threshold | Unload pulses until below 95% |
| 15 | Normal stop | Slide valve unloads, then stop |
| 16 | Open the signal wire (below 3.6 mA) on each of PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103, II-104 | Instrument fault alarm; trip where specified |
| 17 | AE-110A at 25 ppm; repeat for AE-110B | Alarm; EF-201 high speed; compressor continues |
| 18 | AE-110A at 150 ppm; repeat for AE-110B | All compressors stop; XV-120 de-energized; latched |
| 19 | Reduce ppm below the alarm level | ESD remains latched until manual reset |
| 20 | Break-glass pressed with the PLC running | ESD, XV-120 closed, compressors stopped |
| 21 | Break-glass pressed with PLC power removed | Compressor stop and XV-120 de-energized by the hardwired circuit |
| 22 | Break-glass wire disconnected | Treated as activated |
| 23 | Power loss and restoration | No automatic restart; trip and start history retained |
| 24 | Operator, supervisor, and engineering access | Each level restricted as in Section 11 |

## 14. Open Items for Owner/Integrator Confirmation

1. Slide valve position feedback: is there a transmitter?
2. Detector voting: 1oo2 (assumed) or 2oo2? Action on both detectors failing.
3. EF-201 behavior on break-glass and its stop criteria.
4. XV-120 re-open: manual (assumed) or automatic.
5. Behavior on active unloading at alarm conditions, and the motor current unload threshold.
6. Soft starter start limit: a count or thermal model.
7. Low suction trip: bypass at start and trip delay.
8. Package-supplied protections (oil pump, high motor winding temperature, vibration, high discharge pressure/mechanical relief, oil level, and similar). These are not in the given process information and are likely to be required, so please provide them to add to Section 8.
9. Behavior of other compressors in the room during a C-101 trip (for example, start of a standby).
10. Automatic start/stop differentials and times.
